name: Asia
blurb: From Thailand's islands to Vietnam's limestone bays — the region most Indian travellers reach first, and the one that rewards a second visit most.
intro: Asia is the easiest first international trip from India: short flights, visa-on-arrival in much of it, and a cost of travelling that leaves room to stay longer. We cover it as places worth several days, not as country checklists.

name: Middle East
blurb: Desert geology and cities built at speed — a few hours from India and increasingly the region people stop over in rather than fly past.
intro: The Middle East has become a genuine destination rather than a transit lounge. Design-led hotels, desert landscapes and a hospitality culture that changes how you think about being a guest.

name: Europe
blurb: Short distances, deep history, and some of the most walkable cities anywhere.
intro: Europe is the easiest continent to travel slowly. Rail makes multi-country journeys practical, and the difference between a good trip and a great one is usually the base town, not the number of countries.

name: Africa
blurb: Wildlife on a scale that resets your sense of proportion, alongside some of the world's great craft cities.
intro: Africa spans 54 countries and no single itinerary style. We cover it as two travel modes: the wildlife journey, which is logistics-heavy and season-driven, and the city-and-craft journey, which rewards independent travel.

name: North America
blurb: Road-trip country: national parks, mountain towns and food cities with real depth.
intro: Best travelled by car and by region rather than by country. The distances are the story — plan fewer places and longer stays.

name: South America
blurb: Andean altitude, Patagonian wind and some of the last genuinely wild trekking on earth.
intro: South America asks more of travellers than most regions — altitude, distance, weather — and returns more. Build in buffer days.

name: Oceania
blurb: Compact, dramatic and outdoors-first — fiords, alpine lakes and long empty coastlines.
intro: The region where landscape density is highest per kilometre driven.

name: Himalayan North
blurb: The high country — Char Dham, hill stations, paragliding ridges and the tiger forests below them.
intro: India's mountain states, where the season decides everything. Roads open and close, shrines open and close, and the difference between a good trip and a difficult one is almost always timing.

name: North & the Plains
blurb: The temple towns, the Braj country, the Golden Temple and the capital — the densest concentration of pilgrimage travel in the country.
intro: This is where most of India's spiritual travel happens: Ayodhya, Vrindavan, Barsana, Amritsar, and the Rajasthan shrine circuit. It is also the most poorly documented in English, which is exactly why we cover it properly.

name: West India
blurb: Coastline, the two cities that never stop, and the Western Ghats behind them.
intro: The Arabian Sea coast and the metros that grew along it. Goa for the shoreline, Mumbai and Pune for the cities.

name: Central India
blurb: Ancient temple cities and some of the country's best-kept wildlife parks.
intro: The middle of the country, and the part most itineraries skip. Ujjain's Mahakaleshwar anchors it.

name: South India
blurb: Backwaters, tea country, temple architecture and the cities that power the country.
intro: A different India entirely — different food, different scripts, different rhythm. It travels slowly and rewards it.

name: East & Northeast
blurb: Living root bridges, tea gardens and the least-travelled corner of the country.
intro: India's least visited region and its greenest. Distances are short and roads are slow.
